findings: Rare isolated premature ventricular complexes (under 1% burden), benign. No sustained arrhythmia, no pauses greater than 2 seconds, no AV block.
cardiac_monitoring.impression: 24-hour Holter monitor with only benign findings.
cardiac_monitoring.rhythm_summary: Predominant sinus rhythm throughout the recording

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass or large-territory infarct. Prominent lateral ventricles and periventricular white matter hypodensity; MRI is better suited to characterize them.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

findings.test: Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test - Immediate
Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test - Delayed

output.impression: 1. Severe verbal memory impairment: RAVLT immediate recall 28 words over 5 trials and delayed recall 2 words, a storage-type pattern. 2. Mildly impaired naming (Boston Naming Test 48/60) and clock drawing (3/5). 3. Processing speed and set-shifting within age norms (Trail Making A 58 s, B 142 s). 4. Borderline mood screen (GDS 6/15). Screening MMSE 23/30, MoCA 19/30. Multi-domain cognitive impairment with amnestic predominance, at a level consistent with mild dementia given the reported functional decline.

findings.result: Slow gait with shortened stride, mildly wide base and turns requiring multiple steps; tandem walking difficult; no freezing, festination or rigidity.
40 mL of CSF removed at lumbar puncture; timed walking and MMSE repeated at 2 and 24 hours.

output.impression: Slow gait (10 m in 18.2 s) with short stride and multistep turns. After removal of 40 mL of CSF, walking time 17.5 s at 2 h and 17.8 s at 24 h and MMSE unchanged at 23/30: no meaningful improvement in gait or cognition on the tap test.

pre_post_comparison.10 m walk time: 18.2 s before, 17.5 s at 2 h, 17.8 s at 24 h (improvement under 5%)
pre_post_comparison.Gait pattern: Short stride, mildly wide base and multistep turns before and after; no change in turning or tandem walking

output.interpretation: Normal opening pressure (12 cmH2O), cell count, protein and glucose. Decreased Abeta42 and Abeta42/40 ratio with elevated p-tau181 and total tau: a CSF profile consistent with Alzheimer disease pathology. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.region: Frontal, lateral temporal, parietal and posterior cingulate/precuneus cortex
findings.signal: Cortical tracer retention extending to the cortical surface in several regions bilaterally, with loss of grey-white matter contrast

output.impression: POSITIVE amyloid PET: cortical tracer retention in multiple regions (Centiloid 58), indicating moderate to frequent neuritic amyloid plaque density.

interactions: Donepezil + Pantoprazole: no clinically significant interaction; proton pump inhibitors do not reduce donepezil absorption.
Donepezil + Amlodipine: no significant interaction; amlodipine does not slow the heart rate.
Donepezil + Acetaminophen or calcium carbonate with vitamin D: no significant interaction.
warnings: Cholinesterase inhibitors can cause bradycardia, heart block and syncope; check pulse before starting and after dose increases (heart rate 72 bpm at this visit), and review falls, since she already has near-falls.
Nausea, diarrhoea, anorexia, weight loss and vivid dreams are common at initiation; start at 5 mg and increase to 10 mg after 4 to 6 weeks if tolerated.
Avoid adding anticholinergic medicines, which oppose the effect of cholinesterase inhibitors.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic impairment on the MMSE with no cue benefit, informant-confirmed decline over five months, and loss of instrumental independence (missed appointments, unpaid bills needing her daughter's intervention)
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive assessment with informant history, a per-domain profile and an explicit account of daily function
action_criteria.rationale: She minimizes her symptoms and lives alone, so her daughter's account of missed appointments and unpaid bills decides the stage and the safety plan [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Severe storage-type verbal memory impairment with mild naming and clock deficits and processing speed and set-shifting within age norms
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the profile and set a baseline
action_criteria.rationale: A storage-type amnestic profile points to Alzheimer disease, whereas normal pressure hydrocephalus and small vessel disease produce slowing and executive deficits with better recall [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No reversible cause; fasting glucose 108 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.1% above range
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid, B12, folate, syphilis and HIV must be excluded, and metabolic vascular risk measured [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Medial temporal atrophy (MTA 2), Fazekas grade 2 white matter disease, and ventriculomegaly (Evans 0.32) without DESH and with an obtuse callosal angle
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with a dementia protocol to assess medial temporal atrophy, small vessel disease and ventricular size and exclude a mass
action_criteria.rationale: Cognitive decline with a new gait disorder needs MRI to look for normal pressure hydrocephalus (Evans index, DESH, callosal angle) and small vessel disease as well as Alzheimer-type atrophy [iNPH_2005].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No meaningful change in timed walking or MMSE after removal of 40 mL of CSF
action_criteria.label: Consider a timed gait assessment with a high-volume lumbar tap test because of ventriculomegaly and a gait disorder
action_criteria.rationale: With a gait disorder and an Evans index above 0.3, timed gait before and after CSF removal tests for a shunt-responsive component; a negative test lowers but does not exclude normal pressure hydrocephalus [iNPH_2005] [iNPH_Japan_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and here it weighs Alzheimer disease against hydrocephalus and small vessel disease as the main cause; CSF can be drawn at the tap-test puncture [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No clinically significant interaction with pantoprazole, amlodipine, acetaminophen or calcium; bradycardia and syncope risk matter because of her near-falls
action_criteria.label: Check interactions before starting donepezil
action_criteria.rationale: Before a cholinesterase inhibitor her pantoprazole, amlodipine and analgesics should be reviewed, with attention to pulse and falls [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute the decline to normal ageing or poor sleep, as she does; the memory loss is objective and progressive and her function has declined
Do not refer for ventriculoperitoneal shunting on the basis of ventriculomegaly alone, without DESH and after a negative tap test
Do not prescribe a benzodiazepine or Z-drug for her fragmented sleep, given her near-falls and cognitive impairment [Beers_2023]
Do not start memantine at the mild dementia stage; it is indicated for moderate or severe Alzheimer dementia [NICE_NG97]
required_recommendations: Obtain collateral history from an informant who knows the patient well; she minimizes her symptoms
Disclose the diagnosis of mild Alzheimer dementia with cerebrovascular copathology to her and her daughter, and plan durable power of attorney and advance directives
Address safety for a woman living alone: her daughter or a formal arrangement to take over bills and appointments, supervised medicines, and a review of whether she needs more support at home
Refer for physiotherapy gait and balance assessment and a home falls-risk assessment because of near-falls

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].
Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines [NICE_NG97].
Manage vascular risk: bring blood pressure to target (142/84 mmHg today on amlodipine), check a lipid profile, and address HbA1c 6.1% with diet and activity

Re-examine gait and continence at follow-up and reconsider normal pressure hydrocephalus (extended lumbar drainage or neurosurgical opinion) if gait worsens or urinary symptoms appear, since a negative tap test does not exclude it [iNPH_2005]

avoided_actions.rationale: Echocardiography has no role; she has no cardiac symptoms or embolic event
Her near-falls happen while walking, without palpitations, presyncope or loss of consciousness, so cardiac monitoring is not indicated
Head CT adds nothing when MRI is available and cannot assess the hippocampi or DESH as well

accepted: Alzheimer disease (mild dementia, amnestic) with cerebrovascular copathology
mild cognitive impairment due to alzheimer

differential.key_features: Raised by a gait disorder (short stride, wide base, multistep turns) with ventriculomegaly; the full triad is not required. Against it: Evans index 0.32 without DESH, callosal angle 104 degrees, no urinary symptoms, gait for only two months, no meaningful improvement after a 40 mL tap test, and a storage-type amnestic profile with an Alzheimer CSF profile. A negative tap test lowers but does not exclude iNPH, so it is reassessed if gait worsens

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment as the sole cause
differential.key_features: Fazekas 2 small vessel disease with hypertension and raised HbA1c is a real copathology and may contribute to the gait disorder, but the storage-type memory deficit, MTA 2 atrophy and the Alzheimer CSF profile show Alzheimer disease as the primary cause
No visual hallucinations, fluctuations, dream enactment or parkinsonism (no rigidity or bradykinesia); the gait disorder is not parkinsonian
No personality change, disinhibition, compulsions or progressive aphasia; social withdrawal and a glabellar sign are nonspecific; amnestic profile with temporoparietal atrophy
Borderline GDS (6/15) with social withdrawal, but recall is not helped by cues and the deficit is storage-type

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or sleep-related cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV normal; fragmented sleep without features of sleep apnoea

key_clinical_evidence: Missed appointments and unpaid bills needing a relative's intervention are a loss of instrumental independence: the stage is mild dementia, not mild cognitive impairment [NIA_AA_2011]

An Evans index above 0.3 is ventriculomegaly but is not specific for normal pressure hydrocephalus; DESH and an acute callosal angle support it, and a negative tap test lowers its likelihood without excluding it [iNPH_2005] [iNPH_Japan_2021]
Fazekas 2 small vessel disease is a contributing copathology, not an alternative explanation for a storage-type memory deficit with an Alzheimer CSF profile [STRIVE_2013]
One conclusive amyloid biomarker test (CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau, or amyloid PET) is enough [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Normal pressure hydrocephalus does not need the full triad and a negative tap test does not exclude it, so it stays in the differential; but there is no DESH, the callosal angle is obtuse, gait did not improve after the tap test, and the amnestic profile and CSF point to Alzheimer disease as the primary cause
red_herrings.data_point: Ventriculomegaly (Evans index 0.32) on MRI in a patient with memory decline and a new gait disorder
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on normal pressure hydrocephalus and pursue shunting instead of establishing the Alzheimer diagnosis

sequence_constraints.reason: Obtain structural imaging before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect / herniation risk, particularly in older patients
The tap test is a high-volume lumbar puncture: imaging comes first to exclude a mass and to show the ventricles that justify it.
Amyloid biomarkers are interpreted against an established clinical syndrome; they are not a screening test.

findings.result: Alert; oriented to person, place and year but not to the date, and states the month incorrectly.

MMSE 23/30: orientation 8/10, recall 0/3 (none recovered with categorical cues), serial sevens 3/5. Names common objects with word-finding pauses. Clock drawing mildly abnormal with misplaced numbers on the right side.

Her daughter reports five months of repeated questions within a conversation and forgotten phone calls, and social withdrawal from longtime friends. The patient minimizes the problem and attributes it to ageing and poor sleep.

She lives alone. She has missed several scheduled medical appointments and stopped paying utility bills; her daughter discovered the unpaid bills and has had to intervene.

clinical_assessment.impression: MMSE 23/30, with impairment in delayed recall, orientation and attention and a mildly abnormal clock. Free recall 0/3, with no benefit from categorical cues. Her daughter reports five months of progressive memory decline and two months of gait unsteadiness with near-falls. Instrumental independence is lost: she has missed medical appointments and left bills unpaid until her daughter intervened, so the syndrome meets the functional threshold for mild dementia.

Minimal mucosal thickening in bilateral maxillary sinuses (incidental)
Flow voids preserved in major intracranial vessels

findings.location: Bilateral medial temporal lobes and hippocampi

signal_characteristics.T1: Reduced hippocampal volume with widening of choroidal fissures and temporal horns

findings.size: Scheltens medial temporal atrophy score: Grade 2 bilaterally

signal_characteristics.T1: Callosal angle 104 degrees on coronal images at the posterior commissure. High-convexity sulci are not effaced and the Sylvian fissures are proportionate to the cortical sulci: no disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space hydrocephalus (DESH) pattern.
signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: No periventricular signal abnormality to suggest transependymal CSF flow

mri.impression: 1. Bilateral medial temporal atrophy (Scheltens MTA 2; hippocampal volumes below the 15th percentile) with mild symmetric temporoparietal cortical volume loss: pattern supportive of a neurodegenerative process with medial temporal predominance. 2. Ventriculomegaly (Evans index 0.32) without a DESH pattern, with an obtuse callosal angle (104 degrees) and no transependymal flow; nonspecific, and the supportive imaging features of normal pressure hydrocephalus are absent. 3. Periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensities, Fazekas grade 2: moderate cerebral small vessel disease. 4. No acute infarct, haemorrhage or mass. Clinical correlation recommended.

volumetrics.hippocampal_volume: Left 2.8 mL, Right 2.9 mL (below 15th percentile for age and sex)

patient.history_present_illness: This 74-year-old right-handed woman, a retired elementary school teacher, presents to the neurology outpatient clinic with her daughter for evaluation of progressive cognitive decline and gait disturbance over approximately five months. The daughter first noticed subtle changes around five months ago when her mother began repeating the same questions within a single conversation and forgetting recent phone calls. Over the ensuing weeks, the patient reportedly missed several scheduled medical appointments, which was highly uncharacteristic of her previously meticulous organizational habits. Approximately three months ago the patient began having difficulty managing her household finances, resulting in several unpaid utility bills that the daughter discovered incidentally. The patient herself acknowledges some forgetfulness but minimizes the severity, attributing it to normal aging and poor sleep. Her daughter reports that the patient has become more socially withdrawn, declining invitations from longtime friends and spending more time at home alone. Approximately two months ago, the patient developed gait unsteadiness with several near-falls while walking in her apartment, prompting her to stop her daily walking routine. She has not had any witnessed falls with loss of consciousness or head trauma. She denies any episodes of urinary incontinence, visual hallucinations, or fluctuating levels of alertness. There have been no personality or behavioral changes, no compulsive behaviors, and no disinhibition noted by her daughter. The patient reports occasional word-finding difficulty in conversation, particularly when trying to recall names of acquaintances, though she remains conversational and coherent. She denies headaches, fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss. Sleep has been fragmented with frequent awakenings, but there is no history of dream-enactment behavior or restless legs. The patient's primary care physician checked basic labs three months ago and was told everything was normal, though her daughter is uncertain of the specific tests performed. No prior neuroimaging or cognitive testing has been done.

neurological_exam.additional: Frontal release signs: glabellar reflex present (does not habituate after 5 taps), palmomental reflex absent bilaterally. No grasp reflex. Paratonia noted on passive arm movements bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Heel-to-shin testing intact. No intention tremor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive to light. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. Facial sensation and strength symmetric. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline without fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait with shortened stride length, mildly wide-based. Difficulty with tandem walking. Turns require multiple steps. Romberg negative. No festination. Gait initiation intact without freezing.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, and year but not the exact date (states month incorrectly). MMSE score 23/30 (orientation 8/10, losing date and month; recall 0/3; serial 7s 3/5). Able to name common objects but had word-finding pauses. Unable to recall 3 words after 5 minutes even with categorical cues. Clock drawing mildly abnormal with misplaced numbers on right side.
neurological_exam.motor: Strength 5/5 in bilateral upper and lower extremities. No pronator drift. Muscle bulk and tone normal throughout. No rigidity or cogwheeling noted.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric in bilateral upper extremities. 2+ at bilateral knees. 1+ at bilateral ankles. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch and pinprick intact throughout. Proprioception intact at bilateral great toes. Mild decreased vibration sense at bilateral ankles, consistent with age.
